Maya: Heads-up — p95 for /chat/long jumped to ~310ms after the kernel roll this morning. Perf alert triggered. perf-bot posted a runbook.
perf-bot: [alert] p95_slo_breach route=/chat/long p95=310ms threshold=200ms
Jon: Do we have breakdown by tier/pool? dedicated vs hosted?
Maya: Dedicated (g4dn-8) p95=320ms, hosted (g5) p95=240ms. Tails heavier on dedicated. KV hit rate dropped 92% -> 74% for long prompts.
Priya: Did the kernel selector change sequence-length rounding? That can desync KV alignment and spike misses.
Maya: Yes — we switched kernel selector v2.3 to prefer fast-attn-v2 for mid lengths; looks like it mishandles prefix alignment for >512 tokens. Quick profile: 
```
# top hotspot
call_kernel_select(route=\"/chat/long\", seq=1024) -> kernel=fast-attn-v2
KVCache::get_miss_rate() -> 0.26
```
Jon: Two quick levers: revert the selector rule OR reduce token_budget for this route so microbatches are smaller and KV warmups happen more often. Also consider biasing queue policy to dispatch sooner for SLO routes.
Alex: Proposed patch (canary 5%):
```
route_configs[\"/chat/long\"] = {
  token_budget: 24,
  max_queue_ms: 8,
  kv_warmup: true
}
```
Maya: Spun 5% canary with token_budget=24 + kv_warmup. 30m run: p95 -> 165ms, KV hit rate -> 90%. No CPU/GPU cost spike in telemetry.
Priya: Nice. Add regression to eval harness: replay long-chat workload and assert KV_hit_rate >= 88% and p95 < 200ms.
Jon: Also add telemetry: histogram of kernel selection by seq_len bins so we can detect misrouted kernels early.
perf-bot: Created issue INF-4823 with logs, flamegraphs, and canary results. :thumbsup:
Maya: Rolling token_budget change to 50% while we root-cause the selector. Will schedule kernel selector revert + fix in next sprint and follow with postmortem.
Alex: :eyes: ping me if rollback or more canaries needed.
Maya: Thanks folks — dropping perf traces and flamegraphs into the thread for the postmortem.
__note: This document is a single Slack thread; messages are short and in chronological order as required.
